meta.question: Roadmap item #1 claimed the out-of-band ind/dir ratio is caused by too-small a direct reaction volume (0.29 nm) and a blind bump to ~0.5 nm would fix it. Measure the ratio AND the absolute SSB_total vs direct radius on the committed v0.7.0 deposit-site dump, before changing anything.
meta.method: Re-score the committed E33 dump (rad_buf/rade/raddep, N=4096/10 keV) with the accumulated-volume energy-threshold direct scorer at r_direct in {0.29..0.60} nm, deposit-site positions. Indirect is fixed at 201 (chemistry is independent of the direct radius). Deterministic p_break expectation.

finding: The ratio enters PARTRAC's 2-3 band at r_direct ~= 0.40-0.45 nm, BUT the absolute SSB_total simultaneously drifts from 1.28x experiment (Ward 1988, at 0.29 nm) to 1.49-1.60x. So the radius is NOT a free lever: bringing the ratio in-band trades away the (already-validated) absolute yield, AND choosing the radius to land the ratio would be calibration (no verified molecularDNA-source value for ~0.45 nm). This confirms the out-of-band ratio is a TWO-SIDED imbalance, dominated by INFLATED INDIRECT: indirect tripled (64->201) when P_indirect went 0.05->0.13 (parameter-free switch), and the concentrated 21x21 fibre grid over-counts near-backbone OH. E27 showed the OLD-calibrated ratio was 2.24-2.53 in-band across fibre spacing; the parameter-free indirect is what pushed it out.
conclusion: The DNA-damage ratio/absolute gap to Geant4-DNA/PARTRAC is a GEOMETRY problem (concentrated fibre grid inflates indirect), not a direct-radius problem. The honest fix is realistic chromatin geometry (nucleosome -> 30 nm fibre -> nucleus), which removes the concentration artifact and would bring both the ratio and the absolute toward experiment WITHOUT tuning any probability or radius. Roadmap item #1's blind radius bump is REJECTED (calibration + breaks absolute).
status: pass (measured); localizes the damage gap to geometry, rejects the radius knob
